humanNotes: Decision: rejected. Reviewer's BLOCKING finding (RagResponseError object has no attribute code) is factually incorrect: the proposal's __init__(self, message, code=unknown) does set self.code = code. But the reviewer completely missed two real, severe defects it should have caught: (1) from_response()'s branch order is backwards - it checks whether error.message is a string and returns code=message_missing BEFORE ever checking the real error.code field, so for the task's own Example 1 body ({error:{code:dependency_unavailable, message:busy}}) the result is .code == message_missing, not dependency_unavailable, failing the stated example outright; (2) in ask(), raise response_error(response_error.code) calls an already-constructed RagResponseError instance as if it were callable, which raises TypeError: RagResponseError object is not callable on every non-200 response with a truthy error key - the primary case this code exists to handle. First attempt at this task (different, longer task text) failed entirely: the implementer produced a runaway repetition of an identical __init__ definition hundreds of times, which cascaded into a reviewer output that could not be format-corrected and the run errored with no record written; retried with a shorter, simplified task text, which produced this record instead. Neither round of this record is usable. Implemented the fix by hand instead: RagResponseError.__init__ takes code=unknown and stores self.code; a new _error_code() helper mirrors _error_message()'s existing extraction pattern (JSON body -> error dict -> string code field, defaulting to unknown); ask() passes both into RagResponseError at the non-200 branch. Verified against both of the task's own examples directly.
